title: Boomerang uniformity two for F2,1 from q = 307
summary: Decide whether the Mesnager--Wu locally-APN binomial has boomerang uniformity two for every admissible field order from 307; a later preprint claims an infinite counterexample family in characteristic three.

formal_statement.body: Let $q=p^n\ge 307$ be an odd prime power with $q\equiv3\pmod 4$, let $\eta$ be the quadratic character of $\mathbb F_q$, and define $F_{2,1}(x)=x^2(1+\eta(x))$. Must the boomerang uniformity satisfy $\beta(F_{2,1})=2$ for every such $q$? By affine equivalence, the corresponding statement for $F_{2,-1}$ has the same status.

scope.domain: Boomerang uniformity of odd-characteristic locally-APN binomials
assumptions: $q=p^n\ge 307$ is an odd prime power with $q\equiv3\pmod 4$
Boomerang uniformity is defined using the generalized BCT for arbitrary finite-field functions
scope.unresolved_remainder: A later accessible preprint proves that $\beta(F_{2,1})=1$, rather than $2$, whenever $p=3$ and $n\ge3$ is odd, which would refute the universal conjecture on an infinite admissible subfamily. Independent reproduction or peer-reviewed confirmation of that negative resolution claim remains outstanding.

progress.summary: The source reports numerical evidence that its boomerang-uniformity-two theorem should hold for every admissible field order from $q=307$.

An accessible preprint identifies a characteristic-three incompatibility in the source's case analysis and proves $\beta(F_{2,1})=1$ for every odd $n\ge3$, claiming an infinite counterexample family to the universal statement.
